newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn higher on rupiah, supply decline.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn higher on rupiah, supply decline.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were higher on Tuesday on a combination of tight supply and a weaker local currency, with imports expected to be stepped up in September amid fears of a poor harvest.

"The East Java harvest is underway, but arrivals have been smaller than previous years," one trader said. "Although the harvest will only peak after October, I think production will be less because of the dry weather."
A drought sweeping through most parts of the archipelago has the potential to affect the production of several crops if it is prolonged, industry sources said.
"Corn prices have been rising because of tight supply and the weakening of the rupiah against the U.S. dollar over the last two weeks," the trader said.
The Indonesian currency had shed some seven percent against the dollar following offshore speculative attacks, and has in recent days settled at around the 2,600-point level.
Traders said more than 60,000 tonnes of imported corn ordered by three feedmills were scheduled to arrive through August, but added that orders for September were thin.

"Next month we don't see much in the line-up except for one Panamax of 60,000 tonnes," one trader said. "There's not much stocks at hand. My estimate is the trade might not be holding more than 40,000 tonnes as they have been selling continously."
He said players were looking at stepping up imports in September, but added that the orders would come in late August.
"The problem is people (here) don't plan in advance. But when one jumps in everybody else joins in," he added.
"Imports have exceeded 700,000 tonnes so far this year, and are expected to exceed one million tonnes for 1997," he said.
Traders said China was offering September corn at $138-$140 a tonne C&F while Argentine offers were quoted at $147-$147.
They said local corn prices were at 420-430 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 400-410 rupiah a week ago.
They said the soymeal market was quiet, with most players well covered. "I think there is enough meal in the market to last until October," one said.
South American soymeal was offered at $282-$283 C&F a tonne while Indian origin was quoted $302-$305 C&F. Local prices were quoted at 880-890 rupiah/kg against 895-900 rupiah.
